The follow-up native Metal path keeps emulation at that fixed 60 Hz and uses an independent CAMetalDisplayLink, a three-frame immutable queue, one-frame presentation lead, and two 120 Hz draws per source frame. Sharp Bilinear became the fullscreen default, with Smooth and Pixel Sharp retained as explicit choices. Three 780-frame runs remain byte-identical and the presenter reports no producer drops, consumer skips, missing source frames, backward transitions, or starvation. A clean visible sample held 8.333 ms physical intervals and 16.667 ms source transitions, but other current-build visible samples reached approximately 12 ms p99 drawable intervals and approximately 20.5 ms p99 source transitions even while the CPU loop stayed near 16.667 ms. The new dkc1.scanout.v1 trace records actual drawable presentedTime beside camera and BG1-BG3 scroll so the remaining compositor-level variability can be diagnosed without changing game state. September 6: adopted eight-observation refresh qualification with a timestamp fallback, keeping the independent fixed 60 Hz producer. The new five-minute run has zero repeat-goal changes (baseline 116 in 30 seconds), but physical scanout still varies and occluded drawables occur. This remains open; see docs/HOST_ADOPTION_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

issues.mitigation_note: User is independently fixing the Windows host/compositor path. This audit preserves the tested executable and logs without changing that code. A 2.277 ms late frame incurred 31.0844 ms additional wait and a 50.0322 ms interval. Audio-phase elapsed spikes do not isolate whether an OS call or scheduling caused the initial lateness. Physical scanout remains unverified. 2026-09-18 follow-up: the GDI/timer presenter was replaced by the Direct3D 11 flip-model presenter paced by the swap chain waitable object (docs/HOST_PACING.md, Windows presenter). Its DXGI frame statistics are the scanout oracle: in the September 18 captures every present landed on its own refresh except one 33 ms slot in a debug-panel run where the compositor itself held the image for two refreshes, and a one-time 58-81 ms Present at about 1.5 s after the first present (the compositor changing presentation path; DKC1_PRESENT_WARMUP_MS=2500 moves it before frame 1). Remaining outliers are attributable to the compositor/virtual display, not host submission. Later counterbalanced tests supersede the blanket compositor attribution above: a 323 ms message-pump stall was directly identified as WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN, while an audio submission delay and other gaps remain incompletely classified. Async diagnostic writes and complete QPC/ETW API correlation are implemented; queue 1 remains default. Repeated 30-minute soaks were not run after the user deprioritized pacing. The attempted kernel trace failed. See docs/PACING_HARDENING_REVIEW.md; no universal zero-hitch claim.

issues.summary: A thumb that began on Y could not also press B by rolling across the touch diamond; the preceding adapter update handled separate fingers only.
issues.repro: Press Y with one thumb, roll toward B without lifting, roll back to Y, then repeat.
issues.expected: Y stays held, B presses when the same thumb overlaps it, and rolling back releases B for another jump. Double-tap Y hold still works.
issues.evidence: docs/IOS.md; tests/test_ios_touch_button.c; build/ios-roll-tests.log; build/ios-validation/roll-y-b.png; build/ios-roll-install.json; build/ios-roll-launch.json
issues.fixed_note: UIKit keeps a contact with its initial view. Y now forwards per-contact overlap with B using stable layout coordinates and a bounded contact-radius estimate. B combines rolled contributions with its independent direct touches; rolling away or lifting removes only the matching contribution. A release band prevents boundary jitter and a roll invalidates Y double-tap candidacy. The production model passes repeated single-contact Y/B rolls, direct-plus-rolled touches, edge jitter, radius bounds and cancellation; both native Release builds pass. Simulator display QA checks both highlights. Physical thumb feel remains for user playtesting; no runtime/video or save-format changes.

issues.summary: The original UIKit game buttons used transient highlight state for input; the player needs reliable Y+B chords and a double-tap Y hold toggle.
issues.repro: Keep Y pressed and press/release B repeatedly. Double-tap Y, lift the finger, jump with B, then double-tap Y again.
issues.expected: Each button remains independently pressed for its touch lifetime; Y can latch on/off with a visible HOLD indicator.
issues.fixed_note: Track actual UITouch identities and independent button state, explicitly enable concurrent controls, and OR active button masks. Recognize short Y tap pairs without delaying normal button input. Display a green HOLD ring/label and clear input on pause/cancellation. The real input model passes overlapping Y/B presses, repeated jumps, latch on/off, non-latching B taps, long press, drag, multiple fingers and stale release tests. Simulator visible QA and signed device build/install complete; physical touch feel remains for user playtesting. Guest masks, runtime timing and landscape rendering are unchanged.

issues.summary: The first iOS landscape overlay stretched a 256x224 framebuffer to the phone aspect, distorting the game.
issues.repro: Load the iOS game and enter landscape; distortion appeared on the first displayed landscape frame.
issues.expected: Render additional native source columns, preserve SNES pixel proportions, fill the phone with transparent touch controls.
issues.fixed_note: The UIKit host selects an even display-matched source width, 418x224 on iPhone 16 Pro Max, bounded by the existing 448-column PPU capacity. Rebind the framebuffer pitch on geometry changes; present at fixed 7:6 pixel aspect with nearest sampling. Gameplay enters landscape automatically. Native-center exact-state comparisons and six cross-platform replays pass; all 27 samples across four tested transitions pass. Four available clean entrances pass terrain grades and repeat determinism; native-wide machine differences remain investigations and the 40-entrance floor is incomplete. Desktop presets are unchanged. No ROM, generated code, submodule, shared calibration or gameplay-policy edits.

issues.summary: The initial UIKit device build traps before the first game frame on iOS 27 because it creates an application window without adopting scene lifecycle.
issues.repro: Launch the initial signed arm64 build on iPhone 16 Pro Max running iOS 27.0 (24A5408d). The iOS 26.5 simulator does not enforce the requirement.
issues.expected: Create the native window through UIWindowScene and boot the verified game normally.
issues.fixed_note: The crash names ___UIApplicationEvaluateRuntimeIssueForNoSceneLifecycleAdoption_block_invoke. Add a single Game scene declaration, DKCSceneDelegate, and initWithWindowScene. The corrected app boots and remains running on the same phone; the live intro and touch interface were inspected via QuickTime. Three iOS and desktop fresh Jungle replays match all seven frame/memory/audio fingerprints. No game, ROM, saved-state, or widescreen changes. Whole-game mobile performance and physical Bluetooth controllers are not yet validated.
